title: Fallback queue starvation during canary swap caused prolonged degraded serving; pinned version blocked auto-fallback
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Summary: During a scheduled model canary swap (canary -> stable) for a commonly used LLaMA-derived variant, we experienced a partial outage across two regions. The canary rollout coincided with an autoscaler decision that shrank the fallback pool; combined with a version-pinning policy on the stable route, automatic rollback/fallback logic could not re-route traffic to a compatible variant. The immediate symptom was large tail latency and queue timeouts on the fallback queue, causing upstream request failures and higher error rates for customer requests that hit the new variant. Impact window ~2026-03-10T15:12Z -> 2026-03-10T15:48Z.
timeline: 2026-03-10T15:05Z - Canary swap initiated via console rollout: canary v3.2 -> traffic 20%
2026-03-10T15:10Z - Autoscaler executed an aggressive downsize in region-us-central to reclaim GPUs (policy: eager-burst reclaim)
2026-03-10T15:12Z - Observability alert: fallback-queue-depth increased above SLO threshold; tail latencies rising
2026-03-10T15:18Z - Error rate on stable route increased to 6.8% (SLO 0.5%); several customer requests degraded
2026-03-10T15:22Z - On-call attempted automated fallback but hit 'version_pinned' policy on the stable route; auto-fallback aborted
2026-03-10T15:26Z - Manual intervention: engineers attempted manual reroute; traffic remained partially queued due to depleted fallback workers
2026-03-10T15:36Z - Decision to pause rollout and manually spin up extra fallback workers in region-us-central
2026-03-10T15:48Z - Error rates returned to baseline after workers online and manual reroute; rollback avoided but degraded window lasted ~36 minutes
root_causes: Concurrent autoscaler downsize reduced available fallback capacity at the exact time of canary traffic increase
Rollout policy allowed version pin to prevent evicting stable variant, blocking the automated fallback path
Fallback queue lacks backpressure propagation to autoscaler and route controller (no fast-path scaling or emergency bursts)
Insufficient instrumentation linking rollout events, autoscaler actions, and queue depth spikes for automated decisioning
impact_summary: Customer-facing error rates spiked to ~6.8% in affected regions for ~36 minutes
Several enterprise customers reported increased latency impacting inference SLAs; one customer created a Sev2 support case
Billing unaffected; no data exfiltration or security incidents observed
mitigation_taken: Manually paused the canary rollout from Console at 15:36Z
Provisioned emergency fallback workers in region-us-central and region-eu-west via dedicated pool (manual scale-up)
Adjusted route policy to temporarily remove version_pin preventing fallback (manual override) so rollback/fallback could proceed if needed
Post-incident: instituted temporary schedule block on aggressive autoscaler reclaim during active rollouts
action_items: (A1) Implement emergency backpressure signal: route controller should signal autoscaler to pause reclaim when fallback queue depth > threshold — owner: Priya Nair — due: 2026-03-20
(A2) Add a rollout-aware autoscaler policy toggle that prevents downsizing of fallback pools for 10 minutes after any canary traffic change — owner: Daniel Park — due: 2026-03-24
(A3) Update rollout logic to prefer 'graceful drain + provisional burst' rather than relying on version_pin to avoid blocking automated fallback — owner: Lina Chen — due: 2026-03-27

(A4) Improve observability: create a composite dashboard linking rollout events, autoscaler decisions, fallback queue depth, and route policy violations — owner: Observability Team (Ravi Singh) — due: 2026-03-18
(A5) Run a simulated exercise (chaos test) that concurrently triggers canary ramp and aggressive autoscaler reclaim to validate protections — owner: SRE (Aisha Khan) — due: 2026-04-01
(A6) Formalize 'rollout protection' runbook steps for on-call (include exact console paths, emergency scale commands, and communication templates) — owner: Priya Nair — due: 2026-03-16
decisions: Short-term: block aggressive autoscaler reclaim during active rollouts until A1/A2 completed
Medium-term: change default rollout profiles to include a 10-minute 'stabilization hold' preventing trimming of fallback capacity
Long-term: product-level change to support 'emergency fallback burst' in Dedicated capacity contracts (proposal to PM)

notes: This incident exposed a cross-system race: decisions made by the autoscaler are not visible to rollout logic in real time. We should prioritize visibility and simple protective heuristics rather than complex distributed transactions.
Keep customer comms concise: explain root cause as capacity interplay and control-plane policy interaction; avoid deep infra terminology for external notices.
